cards.front: What is matter?
cards.back: Anything that has mass and occupies space
cards.explain: Air, water, food and even our body are matter.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: Air is not matter because we cannot see it.

blank.text: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies ___.

cards.front: What are the tiny particles that matter is made of?
cards.explain: Matter is made of molecules, and molecules are made of even tinier atoms.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: What is the basic building block of all matter?
cards.explain: Two or more atoms join together to form a molecule.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: Atoms can be seen with the naked eye.

blank.text: Two or more ___ join together to form a molecule.

cards.front: What is the space between two molecules called?
cards.explain: It is smallest in solids and largest in gases.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: What is the amount of matter in a body called?
cards.explain: The amount of space an object occupies is its volume.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: What is the amount of space an object occupies called?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: What are the three states of matter?
cards.explain: The difference between them lies in how their molecules are arranged.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: In which state of matter are molecules most tightly packed?
cards.explain: Strong attraction holds the molecules of a solid close together, so they cannot move.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: In solids, the molecules are loosely packed.

blank.text: In ___, the molecules are tightly packed.

cards.front: In which state is the force of attraction between molecules the least?
cards.explain: Gas molecules have a lot of free space and move freely in all directions.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: Why does a solid have a fixed shape and size?
cards.back: Its molecules are tightly packed and cannot move
cards.explain: Strong attraction keeps the molecules in place.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: Solids can be compressed easily.

cards.front: Why do liquids flow?
cards.explain: Liquid molecules are more loosely packed than in solids, so they slide past each other.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

blank.text: Liquids flow from a ___ level to a lower level.

cards.front: A liquid has a fixed volume. Does it have a fixed shape?
cards.back: No – it takes the shape of its container
cards.explain: Water in a glass and in a bottle has different shapes but the same volume.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: No – and no fixed volume either

tf.text: Liquids have a fixed volume but no fixed shape.

cards.front: Which state of matter can be compressed to a large extent?
cards.explain: Gases have lots of free space between molecules – that is why we can fill so much air into a balloon or tyre.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: What is solubility?
cards.back: The ability of a substance to dissolve in another substance
cards.explain: Sugar has high solubility in water.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: The ability to float on water

cards.front: The substance that dissolves is called the …?
cards.explain: In salt water, salt is the solute.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

blank.text: A substance that dissolves in another substance is called a ___.

cards.front: The substance in which the solute dissolves is called the …?
cards.explain: In salt water, water is the solvent.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: Salt + water gives salt water. What is salt water called?
cards.explain: Solute + solvent = solution.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: What is a uniform solution?
cards.back: A solution where the solute spreads evenly through the solvent
cards.explain: Salt breaks into molecules that spread evenly between the water molecules.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: A solution with lumps at the bottom
A solution that cannot be poured

cards.front: Sand, chalk powder and tea leaves do not dissolve in water. What are they called?
cards.explain: Salt and sugar, which dissolve, are soluble substances.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: Sugar is an insoluble substance.

cards.front: Liquids that dissolve easily in water, like milk, are called …?
cards.explain: Milk, glycerine and alcohol are miscible with water.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: Oil floats on water and does not mix. Oil is a … liquid.
cards.explain: Oil and petrol are immiscible with water.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: Oil is miscible in water.

cards.front: Why do bubbles come out when we open a bottle of soda?
cards.back: Carbon dioxide dissolved under pressure escapes
cards.explain: Soda has carbon dioxide dissolved in it under high pressure – this gives the fizz.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: Oxygen is made inside the bottle

tf.text: Carbon dioxide does not dissolve in water.

cards.front: How do fish breathe under water?
cards.back: They use oxygen dissolved in water
cards.explain: Gases like oxygen and carbon dioxide dissolve in water. Aquatic plants use the dissolved carbon dioxide to make food.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: They come up for air every minute

cards.front: Why is water called the universal solvent?
cards.back: It can dissolve more substances than any other liquid
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

blank.text: Water is known as the universal ___.

cards.front: A solid changing into a liquid on heating is called …?
cards.explain: Ice melting into water is an example.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: Melting of ice is a chemical change.

cards.front: A liquid changing into a gas on heating is called …?
cards.explain: Wet clothes dry because the water evaporates.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: A liquid changing into a solid on cooling is called …?
cards.explain: Water kept in the freezer turns into ice.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

blank.text: Water kept in the freezer turns into ice. This is called ___.

cards.front: A gas changing into a liquid on cooling is called …?
cards.explain: Water drops form outside a cold glass because water vapour in the air condenses. Dew forms the same way.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: What happens to the molecules of a substance when it is heated?
cards.back: They gain energy and move faster
cards.explain: On cooling, molecules lose energy and slow down.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: They lose energy and slow down

tf.text: The movement of molecules increases on cooling.

cards.front: Most solids get bigger when heated. What is this called?
cards.explain: On cooling, solids contract (get smaller) as their molecules come closer.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

blank.text: Most solids ___ on heating and contract on cooling.

cards.front: What is a physical change?
cards.back: A temporary change where no new substance is formed
cards.explain: It is usually reversible, like water ↔ ice.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: A permanent change that forms a new substance
A change that can never be reversed
A change only in living things

tf.text: Physical change is a permanent change.

cards.front: What is a chemical change?
cards.back: A permanent change where new substances are formed
cards.explain: Burning leaves gives ash, which is very different from leaves.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: A temporary change with no new substance
A change that is easy to reverse

blank.text: A change that produces new substances is called a ___ change.

cards.front: Melting chocolate in a pan – physical or chemical change?
cards.explain: The melted chocolate can set again – no new substance is formed.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: Baking a cookie – physical or chemical change?
cards.explain: Baked dough cannot turn back into raw dough – new substances form.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: Rusting of an iron nail – physical or chemical change?
cards.explain: Rust is a new substance and the change cannot be reversed.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: Rusting of iron is a chemical change.

cards.front: Making a boat from paper – physical or chemical change?
cards.explain: Only the shape changes; you can unfold it back.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: Burning a candle involves which kind of change?
cards.explain: Wax melting is physical; wax burning to give heat, light and gases is chemical.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: How does the smell of food cooking in the kitchen spread through the whole house?
cards.back: Gas molecules move freely in all directions
cards.explain: The aroma is carried by gas molecules that spread out to fill the space.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: The smell travels through the walls

cards.front: What is the blanket of air around the Earth called?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Which gas makes up most of the air?
cards.explain: About 78% of air is nitrogen and about 21% is oxygen.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

tf.text: Oxygen is the gas found most in air.

cards.front: Which gas in air do we need to breathe?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Which gas do plants take in to make food?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: The lowest layer of the atmosphere, where we live, is the …?
cards.explain: Weather happens in this layer.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Which layer protects us from the Sun's harmful ultraviolet rays?
cards.explain: It is in the stratosphere.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: A blown-up balloon shows that air …?
cards.explain: Air also has weight and exerts pressure.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

tf.text: Air has weight.

cards.front: About how much of the Earth's surface is covered with water?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Letting mud settle at the bottom of a glass of water is called …?
cards.explain: Pouring off the clear water after that is decantation.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Which method kills germs in water at home?
cards.explain: Water is also cleaned with chlorine tablets (chlorination).
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Rocks formed when hot molten magma cools down are called …?
cards.explain: Granite and basalt are igneous rocks.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Rocks formed from layers of sand, mud and pebbles pressed together are …?
cards.explain: Sandstone and limestone are sedimentary rocks.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Rocks changed by great heat and pressure are called …?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Marble is formed from which rock?
cards.explain: The Taj Mahal is made of marble.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: In which type of rock are fossils usually found?
cards.explain: Remains of plants and animals get trapped in the layers.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

tf.text: Fossils are usually found in igneous rocks.

cards.front: What are rocks made of?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: What is the hardest mineral?
cards.explain: Talc is the softest mineral.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Hot liquid rock inside the Earth is called …?
cards.explain: When it comes out of a volcano it is called lava.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Rocks from which metals are taken out are called …?
cards.explain: Iron is taken out of iron ore.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: The slow breaking down of rocks by wind, water and heat is called …?
cards.explain: Weathering of rocks forms soil.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

chapters.title: Force and Energy
pairs: Opening a door away from you

cards.front: A push or a pull is called a …?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Which force pulls everything towards the Earth?
cards.explain: That is why a ball thrown up comes down.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Which force slows down a ball rolling on the ground?
cards.explain: Friction acts between two surfaces that rub.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: The force we use to lift a bag with our hands is …?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Which of these can a force NOT do: move, stop, change shape, or create energy from nothing?
cards.explain: A force can move, stop, speed up, slow down or change the shape or direction of an object.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: What is the ability to do work called?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: What is the main source of energy on Earth?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: A bulb changes electrical energy into …?
cards.explain: It also gives some heat.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: The energy stored in food and batteries is …?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: The energy of a moving object is called …?
cards.explain: Stored energy due to position is potential energy.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

tf.text: A rolling ball has kinetic energy.

cards.front: The spinning of the Earth on its axis is called …?
cards.explain: It takes about 24 hours.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: What causes day and night?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: How long does the Earth take to go once around the Sun?
cards.explain: The extra ¼ day adds up to a leap year every 4 years.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: The Earth moving around the Sun is called …?
cards.explain: Revolution and the tilt of the Earth cause seasons.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: The path the Earth follows around the Sun is its …?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: What is the Moon to the Earth?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Does the Moon make its own light?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title
wrong: Yes – it glows like the Sun
No – it reflects light from the Earth's cities

tf.text: The Moon has its own light.

cards.front: The different shapes of the Moon we see in a month are called …?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: On which night can we not see the Moon at all?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: The Sun is a …?
cards.explain: It is the star nearest to us.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: When the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth, it causes a …?
cards.explain: When the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon, it is a lunar eclipse.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Objects that give out their own light are called …?
cards.explain: The Sun, a candle flame and a bulb are luminous.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Is the Moon luminous or non-luminous?
cards.explain: It only reflects sunlight.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Objects that let all light pass through them, like clear glass, are …?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Objects that let some light pass through them, like butter paper, are …?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Objects that do not let any light pass through them are …?
cards.explain: Wood, stone and books are opaque.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: How does light travel?
cards.explain: That is why opaque objects make shadows.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

tf.text: Light can bend around an opaque object.

cards.front: What is needed to make a shadow?
cards.back: A light source, an opaque object and a screen
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: When is your shadow the shortest?
cards.explain: The Sun is overhead at noon.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: The bouncing back of light from a shiny surface is called …?
cards.explain: A mirror reflects light.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: On which side of the object is its shadow formed?
cards.back: The side away from the light
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Harmful substances that make air, water or soil dirty are called …?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Smoke from vehicles and factories causes …?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Throwing garbage and sewage into rivers causes …?
cards.explain: Polluted water can spread diseases like cholera.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Loud sounds of horns and loudspeakers cause …?
cards.explain: Sound is measured in decibels (dB).
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Waste that rots naturally, like fruit peels, is called …?
cards.explain: Plastic and glass are non-biodegradable.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

tf.text: Plastic is biodegradable.

cards.front: What are the 3 Rs that help reduce pollution?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Which cleaner fuel is used in many buses to reduce air pollution?
cards.explain: CNG stands for Compressed Natural Gas.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Chemicals sprayed on crops to kill pests can cause …?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Planting trees helps reduce air pollution because trees …?
cards.back: Take in carbon dioxide and give oxygen
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Most plants grow from …?

cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: What does a seed need to germinate?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

tf.text: A seed needs sunlight to germinate.

cards.front: Which part of a seed protects it?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Which part of the potato grows into a new plant?
cards.explain: A potato is a stem that stores food.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: What is a young plant growing from a seed called?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Which part of the seed stores food for the baby plant?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Seeds of cotton and dandelion are carried by …?
cards.explain: They are light and have hair-like parts.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Coconuts spread to new places by …?
cards.explain: They float on sea water.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Growing new plants from parts like stem, leaf or root is called …?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Why do plants need to spread their seeds far away?
cards.back: So that new plants get enough space, light, water and food
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title
wrong: So the parent plant can rest

cards.front: Pea and balsam pods burst open to throw out seeds. This is dispersal by …?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Which plant grows new plants from the edges of its leaves?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Ferns and mosses do not make seeds. How do they reproduce?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Why does a seed kept in a dry, airtight box not germinate?
cards.back: It has no water or air
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Animals that live on land are called …?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Animals that live in water are called …?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Animals that can live both on land and in water are called …?
cards.explain: A frog is an amphibian.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

tf.text: A frog is an amphibian.

cards.front: How do fish breathe?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Special features that help an animal live in its habitat are called …?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: How is a camel adapted to the desert?
cards.back: Long legs, a hump that stores fat, and thick eyelashes
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: How is a polar bear adapted to the cold?
cards.back: Thick white fur and a layer of fat
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Animals that live mostly on trees are called …?
cards.explain: Monkeys and squirrels are arboreal.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Why do ducks have webbed feet?
cards.back: To swim and paddle in water
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Why does a fish have a streamlined body?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Why are birds' bones hollow?
cards.back: To make their bodies light for flying
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title
wrong: To make them strong for digging

cards.front: Some animals sleep through the cold winter. What is this called?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: A chameleon changes colour to match its surroundings. This is called …?
cards.explain: It helps it hide from enemies and catch prey.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Why do some birds fly to warmer places in winter?
cards.back: To find food and escape the cold – this is migration
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Which nutrient gives us energy?
cards.explain: Rice, wheat and potatoes are rich in carbohydrates.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Which nutrient helps our body grow and repair itself?
cards.explain: Pulses, milk, eggs and fish are rich in proteins.

cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Why do we need roughage?
cards.back: It helps digestion and prevents constipation
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

tf.text: Roughage gives us a lot of energy.

cards.front: Lack of vitamin C causes …?
cards.explain: Gums bleed. Citrus fruits are rich in vitamin C.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Lack of vitamin D causes …?
cards.explain: Bones become soft. Sunlight helps the body make vitamin D.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Lack of vitamin A causes …?
cards.explain: Carrots are rich in vitamin A.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Lack of iodine causes …?
cards.explain: That is why we use iodised salt.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.explain: Lack of iron causes anaemia.

cards.back: It has too much fat, salt or sugar and few nutrients
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Why are vitamins and minerals called protective foods?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.explain: Pickling, drying and salting are other ways of preserving food.

cards.back: Washing after cutting washes away vitamins

cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.explain: 12 pairs = 24 ribs.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Which is the longest bone in the body?
cards.explain: The smallest bone, the stapes, is in the ear.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: The place where two bones meet is called a …?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.explain: It moves in one direction, like a door hinge.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Which type of joint is found at the shoulder and hip?
cards.explain: It lets the arm and leg move in all directions.

cards.explain: It is an involuntary muscle.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Why do muscles work in pairs, like the biceps and triceps?
cards.back: A muscle can only pull, so one bends the arm and the other straightens it
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Tough bands that join muscles to bones are called …?
cards.explain: Ligaments join bone to bone.

cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: What pulls the Inuit sledges over the snow?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: What do the Inuit mainly eat?
cards.explain: Few plants grow there.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Which plants grow in the tundra?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.back: In summer the Sun does not set for months
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.back: Because of the Earth's tilted axis as it goes around the Sun
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: How are seals and walruses protected from the cold?
cards.back: A thick layer of fat called blubber

cards.front: Why do the Inuit wear clothes made of fur and skin?
cards.back: They keep the body very warm

chapters.title: Don Quixote and the Enchanted Helmet
pairs: What you do matters more than what you say
Laughter makes it easy to handle difficult situations
Birds of a feather flock together
People who are similar spend time together
Don't count your chickens before they're hatched
Don't be confident of success till you see the result
It's always better to tell the truth than to lie

cards.front: Who wrote the novel Don Quixote?
cards.explain: Cervantes (1547–1616) was a Spanish author. Spanish is often called "the language of Cervantes".
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: In which century was Don Quixote written?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: Before becoming a writer, Cervantes worked as …?
cards.back: A soldier and a tax collector
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: Who was Don Quixote's squire?
cards.explain: Sancho was a farmer who became Don Quixote's squire.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

tf.text: Sancho Panza was a barber.

cards.front: Why did Don Quixote want to become a knight?
cards.back: He had read stories of the heroic deeds of brave knights
cards.explain: He was inspired by old novels about knights rescuing maidens and battling dragons.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)
wrong: He wanted to marry a princess

cards.front: What was Don Quixote searching for at the start of the story?
cards.explain: He was still bare-headed, as he had not yet found a new helmet.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

blank.text: Don Quixote rode ___ because he had not found a new helmet.

cards.front: On his previous adventure, what had Don Quixote done?
cards.back: Chased windmills, thinking they were giants
cards.explain: Sancho hoped this adventure would not be like the windmill one.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)
wrong: Flown kites, thinking they were birds
Ridden horses, thinking they were dragons

cards.front: What did Don Quixote believe the horseman was wearing?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: Who was Mambrino?
cards.back: A fictional Moorish king in a Spanish poem
cards.explain: His helmet had an idol that sang "Long live the most noble lord Mambrino" when the wind blew through it.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: What was special about Mambrino's helmet?
cards.back: Whoever wore it could never be attacked or defeated
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

tf.text: Whoever wore Mambrino's helmet could never be defeated.

cards.front: Who was the horseman really?
cards.explain: He was the barber of the larger village, riding to visit his patients in the smaller village.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

tf.text: The horseman was a brave knight.

cards.front: What was the barber riding?
cards.explain: Sancho said he saw only a common man riding a grey donkey, much like his own.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: What was the "golden helmet" actually?
cards.explain: It was kept very clean, so it glittered from more than a mile away.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

blank.text: The "helmet" was really the barber's brass ___.

cards.front: Why did the barber carry a brass basin?
cards.back: To catch the blood when he bled sick patients
cards.explain: In those times, people believed illness could be cured by letting out "bad" blood.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: Why was the barber wearing the basin on his head?
cards.back: It was about to rain and he did not want to spoil his new hat
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)
wrong: He thought it was a helmet
He wanted to look like a knight

cards.front: What did Don Quixote do when the barber came near?
cards.back: He charged at him with his lance
cards.explain: He shouted, "Wretch, save yourself or at once surrender the helmet!"
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: How did the barber escape?
cards.back: He jumped off his donkey, leaped over the hedge and ran across the fields
cards.explain: He ran "as swiftly as a deer", and the basin slipped from his head.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)
wrong: He galloped away on his donkey
He fought back with the basin

cards.front: How did Don Quixote explain why the helmet looked like a barber's basin?
cards.back: An enchanter had changed its form
cards.explain: He planned to have it remade into its proper shape by an armourer.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)
wrong: It had been melted in a fire

cards.front: Don Quixote decided to have the helmet remade by …?
cards.explain: An armourer is a maker of weapons and armour.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: What did Sancho want to exchange?
cards.back: His donkey for the barber's donkey
cards.explain: Don Quixote allowed him to exchange only the saddles.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

tf.text: Don Quixote let Sancho exchange the donkeys.

cards.front: Why did Don Quixote not allow Sancho to take the barber's donkey?
cards.back: Knights do not rob those they meet
cards.explain: "Exchange is no robbery," said Sancho, but Don Quixote said the donkey was dear to its master.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)
wrong: The barber came back for it

cards.front: Rocinante was Don Quixote's …?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: What does the proverb "All that glitters is not gold" mean?
cards.back: Not everything that looks attractive is valuable
cards.explain: The glittering "golden helmet" was only a brass basin.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: What does "take to one's heels" mean?
cards.back: To run away from somebody or something
cards.explain: The barber took to his heels when Don Quixote charged at him.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: What does "bare-headed" mean here?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: What does "enchanted" mean?
cards.explain: An enchanter is someone who uses magic to put spells on people.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: What is a lance?
cards.back: A long spear used by a soldier on horseback
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: What does "surrender" mean?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: What is a hedge?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: What is a visor?
cards.back: The front part of a helmet that protects the eyes or face
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: What does "wretch" mean?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: What do adverbs tell us more about?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: "See there!" – what kind of adverb is "there"?
cards.explain: Adverbs of place tell us where: here, nowhere, everywhere, out.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: "A horseman was coming slowly" – what kind of adverb is "slowly"?
cards.explain: Adverbs of manner tell us how, and mostly end in -ly: neatly, quickly, sadly.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: "Yesterday, the knight came across a barber" – what kind of adverb is "yesterday"?
cards.explain: Adverbs of time tell us when: today, tomorrow, recently, soon, now.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: "Could never be attacked" – what kind of adverb is "never"?
cards.explain: Adverbs of frequency tell us how often: always, rarely, sometimes.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

tf.text: Adverbs of frequency tell us where an action happens.

cards.front: What are conjunctions?
cards.back: Joining words that join two or more words or sentences
cards.explain: Examples: and, or, because, for, nor, but, yet, so, since, as.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

blank.text: I want a new cycle, ___ I don't have the money to buy one.

cards.front: Which spelling is correct for a person who writes books?
cards.explain: Words ending in -er and -or sound alike: barber, master, author, collector.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: Why did the barber's basin glitter from more than a mile away?
cards.back: It was always kept very clean
cards.explain: Don Quixote saw the shine and believed it was a golden helmet.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)
wrong: The sun was shining on gold paint

tf.text: The basin glittered because it was made of gold.

cards.front: Which proverb best fits Don Quixote's mistake about the "golden helmet"?
cards.back: All that glitters is not gold
cards.explain: It glittered like gold but was only a brass basin.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: Why was Sancho nervous about the new adventure?
cards.back: Last time, Don Quixote had mistaken windmills for giants
cards.explain: "I pray to God, master, that it isn't like our last adventure."
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)
wrong: He was afraid of the barber

cards.front: Why did Sancho try to hide his laughter when Don Quixote wore the "helmet"?
cards.back: It looked like a barber's basin, but his master was proud of it
cards.explain: Don Quixote grew angry at him for grinning.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: "He ran away as swiftly as a deer." What kind of adverb is "swiftly"?
cards.explain: It tells us how he ran.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: "Wretch, save yourself or at once surrender the helmet." Which word is the conjunction?
cards.explain: "Or" joins the two choices Don Quixote gives the barber.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

cards.front: Complete with -er or -or: "My teacher wants me to be the monit__ of the class."
cards.explain: Rider, baker and swimmer end in -er; monitor and creator end in -or.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 1 (pp. 12–21)

blank.text: J. K. Rowling is the creat___ of the Harry Potter series.

chapters.title: Earrings for Nina
pairs: Pianist who started losing his hearing at 30
Lost a leg but became a dancer and actress
Could not hear properly; invented the light bulb for homes
Lost her sight and hearing; learnt to read with Anne Sullivan
First differently-abled woman to climb Mount Everest

cards.front: Who wrote "Earrings for Nina"?
cards.explain: She writes humorous children's stories full of mystery, translated into Tamil, Bengali, Assamese and Hindi.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: How were Nina and Rekha related?
cards.explain: Rekha was the elder sister; Nina was the younger one.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

tf.text: Nina and Rekha were friends.

cards.front: Why had Nina gone to the jewellery store?
cards.back: To buy earrings for her tenth birthday
cards.explain: Grandma had sent money for both girls to buy earrings for their birthdays.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: Why could Nina not hear?
cards.back: She had a dangerous brain fever two years ago
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)
wrong: She hurt her ears in a fall

tf.text: Nina could not hear after getting a brain fever.

cards.front: How did Nina "hear" what people said?
cards.explain: This is called lip reading. She learnt it at a special school.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

blank.text: Nina learnt to "hear" by watching people's ___ move.

cards.front: What did Rekha make sure of while talking to Nina?
cards.back: That Nina could watch her face
cards.explain: Nina needed to see Rekha's face to read her lips.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: Why did Nina stop going to her old school?
cards.back: She felt sad at the pity in her friends' eyes
cards.explain: She could not understand her teachers and could not take part in music programmes.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: What kind of earrings caught Nina's eye?
cards.explain: At the end, Nina says she wants to come back to buy them.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: What was the store famous for?
cards.explain: Only the store manager could unlock the glass cabinets.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: How many robbers came into the store?
cards.explain: Two men with guns, faces covered with black masks, burst into the room.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

tf.text: There were two robbers in the store.

cards.front: Who was the first to notice the masked men?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

tf.text: Rekha was the first one to notice the masked men.

cards.front: Who was Mrs Verma?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: What did the robbers do right after entering the store?
cards.back: One grabbed the security guard and the other went to the diamond section
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: What happened when the manager reached for the telephone?
cards.back: A robber fired a shot and hurt his hand
cards.explain: He was then forced to unlock the cabinets.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: What was the secret about the manager?
cards.back: He was in league with the robbers
cards.explain: "In league with" means making secret plans with somebody.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

tf.text: The manager was not involved in the robbery.

cards.front: What did the manager warn the robber not to do?
cards.back: Shoot the glass cabinets, as it would set off the alarm
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: Why did the manager think nobody could hear him?
cards.explain: Nina read his lips through the bullet-proof glass.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: How did Nina prove what the manager said?
cards.back: Her special school's principal could watch the store's video tape
cards.explain: The principal could also read lips from the recorded tape.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: What did the inspector say to Nina at the end?
cards.back: The case could be solved only because of her special abilities
cards.explain: He gave Nina a "thumbs up" sign.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: Why did Nina want to come back to the store?
cards.explain: Rekha said she would never set foot in the store again.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: What does "be green with envy" mean?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: What does "catch somebody's eye" mean?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: What does "burst into tears" mean?
cards.explain: "Broke into" a laugh means started laughing.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: What does "scornfully" mean?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: Who are witnesses?
cards.back: People who have seen an event happen
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: What is "chaos"?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: What does "confident" mean?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: What are compound words?
cards.back: Words formed by joining two or more words
cards.explain: ear + rings = earrings; birth + day = birthday
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

blank.text: tooth + brush = ___

cards.front: What is a suffix?
cards.back: A set of letters added at the end of a word to make a new word
cards.explain: kind + ness = kindness; confuse + ion = confusion
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)
wrong: A word at the start of a sentence
A word with the opposite meaning

blank.text: happy + ness = ___

cards.front: Add -ous to "adventure". What is the new word?
cards.explain: Drop the "e" before adding -ous.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: Which tense talks about an action that started in the past and has just been completed?
cards.explain: Rekha has chosen some earrings to buy.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

blank.text: The masked men ___ robbed the store today.

cards.front: Which tense talks about an action that took place before another action in the past?
cards.explain: Two years ago, Nina had got a dangerous brain fever.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

blank.text: He ___ come home but left before anyone woke up.

cards.front: How did Nina find out that the manager was in league with the robbers?
cards.back: She read his lips through the glass while he spoke to a robber
cards.explain: He thought nobody could hear because the room was sound-proof.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)
wrong: She heard him on the phone

cards.front: Why did the manager think his secret was safe?
cards.back: He thought nobody could hear him in the sound-proof glass room
cards.explain: He forgot that the glass let people see his lips move.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: What does Nina's wish to come back to the store show about her?
cards.back: She is brave and not frightened by what happened
cards.explain: Rekha, by contrast, said she would never set foot in the store again.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)
wrong: She wants to meet the robbers
She did not understand the danger

cards.front: Why were Nina, Rekha and Mrs Verma asked to stay after the robbery?
cards.back: They were witnesses and had to give statements
cards.explain: Witnesses are people who have seen an event happen.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)
wrong: They had to pay for earrings

cards.front: Give a sentence from the story in the past perfect tense.
cards.back: Nina had got a dangerous brain fever.
cards.explain: Past perfect = had + past participle.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

cards.front: Make a compound word from "foot" and "path".
cards.explain: foot + path. Kindness and action are made with suffixes.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

blank.text: snow + flake = ___

cards.front: Add -ion to "admit". What is the new word?
cards.explain: Some words change their spelling when a suffix is added.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 English, Ch 2 (pp. 24–33)

chapters.title: Johnny Head-in-Air

tf.text: Johnny always watched his step carefully.

cards.front: What did Johnny like to look at while walking?
cards.back: The sky, the clouds and the birds
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Where did Johnny fall in the end?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Who laughed at Johnny when he fell into the water?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: What did Johnny trip over on his way?
cards.explain: He was looking up, so he did not see the dog in his path.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Who pulled Johnny out of the river?
cards.explain: They used long poles to pull him out.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: What did Johnny lose in the river?

cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: How did Johnny feel when he came out of the river?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Why do you think the fishes laughed at Johnny?
cards.back: A boy falling into the river because he looked at the sky seemed silly to them

cards.front: In "Johnny Head-in-Air", "head-in-air" describes someone who is …?
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Which pair of words rhymes, as in the poem?

cards.front: Who wrote the poem "Call for Peace"?
cards.explain: It is taken from his long poem "The Song of Hiawatha".

cards.front: The poem is taken from which longer work?

cards.front: What did the Great Spirit want the tribes to do?

cards.front: What is a peace-pipe a sign of?

cards.front: Who called the tribes together in the poem?

cards.front: How did the Great Spirit call the tribes?
cards.back: By smoking a peace-pipe, whose smoke rose high as a signal

cards.front: What were the warriors told to do with their war-paint?

cards.back: People should live together as brothers, not fight

cards.front: Why does washing off war-paint stand for peace?

chapters.title: Sudan: The End of a Species

cards.front: Who was Sudan?
cards.back: The last male northern white rhino
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: In which country did Sudan spend his last years?
cards.explain: He lived at the Ol Pejeta Conservancy.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Why are rhinos killed by poachers?
cards.explain: Poaching means illegal hunting.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: When did Sudan die?
cards.explain: He died on 19 March 2018, at the age of about 45.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

tf.text: Sudan died in 2018.

cards.front: What does "extinct" mean?
cards.back: No longer living anywhere on Earth
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: How many northern white rhinos are left after Sudan died?
cards.explain: They are Najin and her daughter Fatu.
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: How was Sudan protected from poachers?
cards.back: Armed guards watched him day and night
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title
wrong: He was kept in a cage underground

cards.front: What is a rhino's horn made of?
cards.back: Keratin, the same material as our hair and nails
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: Why is the northern white rhino called "functionally extinct"?
cards.back: Only two females are left, so they cannot breed naturally
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: What does "species" mean?
cards.back: A group of living things of the same kind that can breed together
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.front: How are scientists trying to save the northern white rhino?
cards.back: By using frozen cells and eggs to create new rhinos
cards.source: Class 5 Term 2 book, written from the chapter title

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 2 (pp. 19–29)

cards.front: मुहावरे 'आँखों का तारा' का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: मोनिका अपने माता-पिता की आँखों का तारा है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 2 (pp. 19–29)

cards.front: मुहावरे 'नौ-दो ग्यारह होना' का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: माँ ने सफ़ाई करने के लिए कहा तो सारे बच्चे नौ-दो ग्यारह हो गए।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 2 (pp. 19–29)

cards.front: मुहावरे 'छक्के छुड़ाना' का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: क्रांतिकारियों ने अंग्रेजी सेना के छक्के छुड़ाए।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 2 (pp. 19–29)

cards.front: 'चिराग जाला उतार रहा था' का वचन बदलने पर वाक्य क्या होगा?
cards.explain: रेखांकित शब्द 'जाला' का बहुवचन 'जाले' है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 2 (pp. 19–29)

cards.front: 'दीये' शब्द का एकवचन क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 2 (pp. 19–29)

cards.front: 'सत्य' का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
cards.explain: विलोम शब्द एक-दूसरे का उलटा अर्थ देते हैं।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 2 (pp. 19–29)

cards.front: 'रेशमा' और 'अयोध्या' संज्ञा के किस भेद के शब्द हैं?

cards.front: 'अच्छाई', 'सत्य' और 'कमी' संज्ञा के किस भेद के शब्द हैं?
cards.explain: भाववाचक संज्ञा गुण, दशा या भाव का बोध कराती है।

cards.explain: मैंने सीखा: शारीरिक कमी पर विजय पाना, साहस को सफलता का आधार बनाना।

cards.front: कुनढेई पुतली की कौन-सी विशेषता उसे राजस्थानी कठपुतली से अलग बनाती है?
cards.explain: यह हलकी लकड़ी से बनी होती है और इसमें अनेक जोड़ होते हैं।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 3 (pp. 32–42)

cards.explain: संचालक लकड़ी के तिकोने फ्रेम को पकड़े रहता है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 3 (pp. 32–42)

cards.front: कर्नाटक की धागा पुतली का नाम क्या है?
cards.explain: ये पुतलियाँ अत्यंत सुसज्जित होती हैं।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 3 (pp. 32–42)

cards.front: गोम्बेयेट्टा पुतली का संचालन कितने धागों से होता है?
cards.explain: इनका संचालन फ्रेम से बँधे धागों से होता है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 3 (pp. 32–42)

cards.explain: इसमें छड़ और धागे का प्रयोग एक साथ मिलता है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 3 (pp. 32–42)

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 3 (pp. 32–42)

cards.explain: इसका संचालन भी काष्ठ से किया जाता है।

cards.explain: उस टोपी से पुतलियों से जुड़ी छड़ें बँधी रहती हैं।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 3 (pp. 32–42)

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 3 (pp. 32–42)

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: "व्यर्थ" का समानार्थक शब्द क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: "कोना-कोना छानो" में "छानो" का क्या अर्थ है?
cards.explain: एक ही शब्द वाक्य के अनुसार अलग अर्थ देता है – "आटा छानो" में छानो का अर्थ ढूँढ़ना नहीं है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: जो शब्द अलग-अलग वाक्यों में अलग-अलग अर्थ देते हैं, वे क्या कहलाते हैं?
cards.explain: जैसे "बस" – स्कूल की बस (वाहन), बस करो (रुको), मेरे बस की बात (वश)।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: "स्कूल की बस आ गई।" इसमें "बस" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: "कर" शब्द के दो अर्थ कौन-से हैं?
cards.explain: कविता में "कर मल-मल पछताता" – यहाँ कर का अर्थ हाथ है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: "मेरी बात ___ नहीं तो पछताओगे।" सही मुहावरा चुनिए।
cards.explain: गाँठ बाँधना = अच्छी तरह याद रखना।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: "मिठाई देखकर रीमा के ___।" सही मुहावरा चुनिए।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: "समय बीत जाने पर कभी ___।" सही मुहावरा चुनिए।
cards.explain: हाथ न आना = प्राप्त न होना।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: "रोटी खोकर वह ___।" सही मुहावरा चुनिए।
cards.explain: हाथ मलना = पछताना।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: धन + वान = ?
cards.explain: इसी तरह बल + वान = बलवान, गुण + वान = गुणवान, दया + वान = दयावान।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

blank.text: बल + वान = ___

cards.front: शब्दों के अंत में जो शब्दांश जोड़े जाते हैं, वे क्या कहलाते हैं?
cards.explain: जैसे "वान", "दान", "ई" – धनवान, श्रमदान, धनी।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: कौन-सी चीज़ एक बार जाने पर वापस नहीं आती?
cards.explain: कमान से निकला तीर और मुँह से निकली बात भी वापस नहीं आती।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: इस कविता से हमें क्या सीख मिलती है?
cards.back: सभी काम समय पर करने चाहिए
cards.explain: मैंने सीखा: समय का मूल्य पहचानना, सभी कार्य समय पर करना, समय को नष्ट न करना।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)
wrong: समय की परवाह नहीं करनी चाहिए

cards.front: कवि विद्या और समय में क्या अंतर बताता है?
cards.back: खोई विद्या दोबारा पाई जा सकती है, पर खोया समय नहीं
cards.explain: "विद्या खो जाती, फिर भी पढ़ने से है आ जाती, लेकिन खो जाने से मिलती नहीं समय की थाती।"
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)
wrong: खोया समय दोबारा मिल जाता है

cards.front: "जीवन भर भटको, छानो, दुनिया का कोना-कोना" – इसका भाव क्या है?
cards.back: पूरी दुनिया ढूँढ़ने पर भी खोया हुआ समय नहीं मिलता
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: "चला गया जो समय, लौटकर कभी नहीं फिर आता" को दूसरे तरीके से कैसे कहेंगे?
cards.back: जो समय बीत गया, वह लौटकर फिर कभी नहीं आता
cards.explain: किसी भी बात को हम कई तरीकों से कह सकते हैं।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: "घड़ी" शब्द के दो अर्थ कौन-से हैं?
cards.back: समय बताने वाला यंत्र और थोड़ा-सा समय
cards.explain: "एक घड़ी के लिए" में घड़ी का अर्थ थोड़ा-सा समय है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: कविता में समय की तुलना किससे की गई है?
cards.explain: "खो जाने से मिलती नहीं समय की थाती।"
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.front: "हाथ मलना" और "हाथ न आना" में क्या अंतर है?
cards.back: हाथ मलना = पछताना; हाथ न आना = प्राप्त न होना
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, poem (pp. 45–48)

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: चाचा जी के अनुसार बच्चे दिन भर क्या करते रहते हैं?
cards.explain: उन्होंने कहा — हमारे ज़माने में कितनी पढ़ाई होती थी।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: बच्चे मेला देखने कैसे गए?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: भूख लगने पर चाचा जी बच्चों को कहाँ ले गए?
cards.explain: वहाँ माँ का दिया घर का खाना खाया।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: सरकस के चार टिकट कितने रुपये के थे?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: मेले में बच्चों ने क्या-क्या खरीदा?
cards.explain: चाचा जी मोल-भाव करके आगे चल दिए।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: ‘हमें मेला देखना है।’ — यह किसने कहा?

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.explain: सब बच्चे सहमते हुए बोले — जी चाचा जी!
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: ‘बेशुमार’ शब्द का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.explain: जैसे — धीरे-धीरे, ऊपर, नौ बजे, खूब।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: ‘मिनी रेल धीरे-धीरे चलती है’ में ‘धीरे-धीरे’ किस प्रकार का क्रियाविशेषण है?
cards.explain: यह क्रिया का तरीका (रीति) बताता है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: ‘झूले पर ऊपर ही लटके रह जाओगे’ में ‘ऊपर’ किस प्रकार का क्रियाविशेषण है?

cards.front: चाट-समोसे, हाथ-पैर, मोल-भाव, उछल-कूद जैसे जोड़े शब्द क्या कहलाते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: पाठ में ‘मोटी’ शब्द व्याकरण की दृष्टि से क्या है?
cards.explain: ‘मोटी नाक’ — नाक की विशेषता बताता है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: चाचा जी मेला पैदल क्यों ले गए?
cards.back: किराए का पैसा बचाने के लिए
cards.explain: उन्होंने कहा पैदल चलने से पैर और पेट मज़बूत होते हैं।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: चाचा जी ने बाहर का खाना खाने के क्या नुकसान बताए?
cards.explain: दस्त, हैजा, खाँसी, बुखार।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: चाचा जी ने मिनी रेल को क्या बताया?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: चाचा जी बच्चों को सरकस क्यों नहीं ले गए?
cards.explain: ठंड, सुनसान रास्ता और चोर-लुटेरे का बहाना बनाया।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: ‘वे जितने छोटे कद के थे, उनका दिल भी उतना ही छोटा था’ — इससे चाचा जी के बारे में क्या पता चलता है?
cards.explain: वे हर खर्च से बचने का बहाना बनाते हैं।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.front: अंत में बच्चे एक-दूसरे का मुँह क्यों देखने लगे?
cards.back: उन्हें मेले का कोई मज़ा नहीं मिला
cards.explain: चाचा जी ने कहा — तुम लोगों ने मेले के मज़े तो खूब लूट लिए, न!
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi reader (संगीत संकलन), Ch 5 (pp. 50–58)

cards.explain: जिस घर में वे रहते थे, वह भी उन्हें फैलू चौधरी से मुफ़्त में मिला था।

cards.explain: बचा खाना अँगोछे में बाँधकर ले जाते और किसी के पूछने पर खाना बरबाद न करने की दुहाई देते।

cards.front: युवकों ने मुफ़्तलाल को किसके बगीचे के आम के बारे में बताया?
cards.explain: युवकों ने कहा कि गाँव के लोग सारे आम तोड़ लेंगे, इसलिए मुफ़्तलाल सुबह होने से पहले ही आम तोड़ने चल दिए।

cards.back: रगड़ से बिजली की धारा पैदा होती है

cards.explain: थाल आकाश है और मोती तारे हैं।

cards.explain: जैसे — पिता जी आ रहे हैं।

tf.text: "गुरु जी आ रहे हैं" में बहुवचन क्रिया आदर के लिए है।

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: संज्ञा या सर्वनाम का क्रिया से संबंध बताने वाले रूप को क्या कहते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: कर्म कारक का चिह्न क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "का, के, की" किस कारक के चिह्न हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "हे! अरे!" किस कारक के चिह्न हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.explain: अलग होने के अर्थ में "से" अपादान है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "वह कलम से लिखता है।" — इसमें "से" किस कारक का है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: संज्ञा के स्थान पर प्रयोग होने वाले शब्द क्या कहलाते हैं?

cards.front: सर्वनाम के कितने भेद होते हैं?
cards.explain: पुरुषवाचक, निश्चयवाचक, अनिश्चयवाचक, प्रश्नवाचक, संबंधवाचक, निजवाचक
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "मैं, तुम, वह" किस प्रकार के सर्वनाम हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "कौन, क्या" किस प्रकार के सर्वनाम हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "कोई, कुछ" किस प्रकार के सर्वनाम हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "यह, वह" (किसी निश्चित वस्तु के लिए) किस प्रकार के सर्वनाम हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "मैं अपना काम स्वयं करता हूँ।" — "स्वयं" कौन-सा सर्वनाम है?

cards.front: "जो करेगा, सो भरेगा।" — "जो, सो" कौन-से सर्वनाम हैं?

cards.front: संज्ञा या सर्वनाम की विशेषता बताने वाले शब्द क्या कहलाते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: जिसकी विशेषता बताई जाती है, उसे क्या कहते हैं?

cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: विशेषण के कितने भेद होते हैं?
cards.explain: गुणवाचक, संख्यावाचक, परिमाणवाचक, सार्वनामिक
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "लाल गुलाब" में "लाल" किस प्रकार का विशेषण है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "चार केले" में "चार" किस प्रकार का विशेषण है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "दो लीटर दूध" में "दो लीटर" किस प्रकार का विशेषण है?
cards.explain: नाप-तौल बताता है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "यह लड़का होशियार है।" — "यह" किस प्रकार का विशेषण है?
cards.explain: सर्वनाम संज्ञा से पहले आकर विशेषण बन जाता है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "भारत" से विशेषण क्या बनेगा?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: जिन शब्दों से किसी काम के करने या होने का पता चले, उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: क्रिया के मूल रूप को क्या कहते हैं?
cards.explain: जैसे — पढ़ना की धातु "पढ़"।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: कर्म के आधार पर क्रिया के कितने भेद होते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: जिस क्रिया के साथ कर्म हो, उसे क्या कहते हैं?
cards.explain: जैसे — राम आम खाता है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "बच्चा हँसता है।" — इसमें कौन-सी क्रिया है?
cards.explain: इसमें कर्म नहीं है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "लिखना" की धातु क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: क्रिया पहचानने के लिए "क्या" से प्रश्न करने पर उत्तर मिले, तो क्रिया कौन-सी होती है?
cards.explain: राम क्या खाता है? — आम (कर्म)।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "माँ ने बच्चे को सुलाया।" — "सुलाया" कौन-सी क्रिया है?
cards.explain: कर्ता स्वयं न करके दूसरे से काम करवाता है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: क्रिया के जिस रूप से काम के होने के समय का पता चले, उसे क्या कहते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: काल के कितने भेद होते हैं?
cards.explain: भूतकाल, वर्तमान काल, भविष्यत् काल
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "मैंने खाना खाया।" — यह किस काल का वाक्य है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "मैं कल दिल्ली जाऊँगा।" — यह किस काल का वाक्य है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "बच्चे खेल रहे हैं।" — यह किस काल का वाक्य है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: भविष्यत् काल के वाक्य प्रायः किन शब्दों पर समाप्त होते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "वह पढ़ता है।" को भूतकाल में बदलिए।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "मैं पत्र लिखूँगा।" को वर्तमान काल में बदलिए।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: जिन शब्दों का रूप लिंग, वचन, कारक के कारण नहीं बदलता, उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: अविकारी शब्दों के कितने भेद होते हैं?
cards.explain: क्रियाविशेषण, संबंधबोधक, समुच्चयबोधक, विस्मयादिबोधक
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: क्रिया की विशेषता बताने वाले शब्द क्या कहलाते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "कछुआ धीरे-धीरे चलता है।" — इसमें क्रियाविशेषण कौन-सा है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "और, परंतु, क्योंकि" किस प्रकार के शब्द हैं?
cards.explain: ये दो शब्दों या वाक्यों को जोड़ते हैं।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "वाह!, अरे!, हाय!" किस प्रकार के शब्द हैं?
cards.explain: ये हर्ष, शोक, आश्चर्य आदि भाव बताते हैं।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "किताब मेज़ के ऊपर रखी है।" — "के ऊपर" किस प्रकार का शब्द है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: संज्ञा, सर्वनाम, विशेषण और क्रिया किस प्रकार के शब्द हैं?
cards.explain: इनका रूप बदलता है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: शब्दों के सार्थक समूह को, जिससे पूरी बात समझ आए, क्या कहते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: वाक्य के कितने अंग होते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: वाक्य में जिसके बारे में बात कही जाए, उसे क्या कहते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "मोहन पुस्तक पढ़ता है।" — इसमें उद्देश्य क्या है?
cards.explain: बाकी "पुस्तक पढ़ता है" विधेय है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "तुम कहाँ जा रहे हो?" — यह किस प्रकार का वाक्य है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "दरवाज़ा बंद करो।" — यह किस प्रकार का वाक्य है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "मैं आज स्कूल नहीं जाऊँगा।" — यह किस प्रकार का वाक्य है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "भगवान तुम्हें लंबी आयु दे।" — यह किस प्रकार का वाक्य है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "शायद आज वर्षा हो।" — यह किस प्रकार का वाक्य है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: समान अर्थ वाले शब्दों को क्या कहते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: उलटा अर्थ बताने वाले शब्दों को क्या कहते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "दिन" का विलोम क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "सूर्य" का पर्यायवाची कौन-सा है?
cards.explain: अन्य — रवि, भानु, दिवाकर
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "जल" का पर्यायवाची कौन-सा है?
cards.explain: अन्य — पानी, वारि, अंबु
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "आकाश" का पर्यायवाची कौन-सा है?
cards.explain: अन्य — नभ, अंबर
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "सुख" का विलोम क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "जो ईश्वर को मानता हो" — इसके लिए एक शब्द क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "जिसका कोई आकार न हो" — इसके लिए एक शब्द क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: "कनक" शब्द के दो अर्थ कौन-से हैं?
cards.explain: एक शब्द के कई अर्थ हों तो वह अनेकार्थी शब्द कहलाता है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), written from the chapter title

cards.front: जो वाक्यांश सामान्य अर्थ न देकर विशेष अर्थ प्रकट करते हैं, उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
cards.explain: मुहावरों से भाषा रोचक और प्रभावशाली बनती है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: मुहावरे वाक्य होते हैं या वाक्यांश?
cards.explain: मुहावरे का प्रयोग वाक्य के भीतर होता है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

tf.text: मुहावरा अपने आप में पूरा वाक्य होता है।

cards.front: लोगों में प्रचलित अनुभव द्वारा प्राप्त उक्ति को क्या कहते हैं?
cards.explain: इसे "कहावत" भी कहा जाता है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "लोकोक्ति" शब्द किन दो शब्दों से मिलकर बना है?
cards.explain: लोक = लोग, उक्ति = प्रचलित बात।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: लोकोक्ति का दूसरा नाम क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

blank.text: लोकोक्ति को ___ भी कहते हैं।

cards.front: कहावतें किस आधार पर बनती हैं?
cards.back: लोगों के अनुभवों के आधार पर
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "ईद का चाँद होना" मुहावरे का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: शिवम पूरे एक महीने बाद दिखा है। वह तो जैसे ईद का चाँद हो गया था।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "जाल में फँसना" मुहावरे का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: सिम्मी अपने भोलेपन के कारण ठग के जाल में फँस गई।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "लोहा लेना" मुहावरे का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "अगर-मगर करना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: दादा जी ने विनय से बाज़ार जाने के लिए कहा, तो वह अगर-मगर करने लगा।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "आँखों में धूल झोंकना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: अपराधी ने पुलिस की आँखों में धूल झोंककर भागना चाहा।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "हवा से बातें करना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: राणा प्रताप का घोड़ा चेतक हवा से बातें करता था।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "नमक-मिर्च लगाना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "काम तमाम करना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: सेना ने कुछ पलों में ही शत्रु का काम तमाम कर दिया।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "चिकना घड़ा" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: मयंक को कुछ समझाना बेकार है, वह तो चिकना घड़ा है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "बाल-बाल बचना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: रेल दुर्घटना में सभी यात्री बाल-बाल बच गए।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "अंग-अंग ढीला होना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "बाएँ हाथ का खेल" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: कंचन के लिए तीन-चार किलोमीटर दौड़ना बाएँ हाथ का खेल है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "कान भरना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: मनीष काम करने की जगह सारा दिन मालिक के कान भरता रहता है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "किताबी कीड़ा" किसे कहते हैं?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "होश उड़ जाना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: पुलिस को देखकर अपराधियों के होश उड़ गए।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "टेढ़ी खीर" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: प्रदूषण से भरे वातावरण में स्वस्थ रहना टेढ़ी खीर है।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "उल्लू बनाना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "चकमा देना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "इतिश्री होना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: "कौन बनेगा करोड़पति" में 50 लाख रुपये जीतने से उनके दुखों की इतिश्री हो गई।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "कान का कच्चा होना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.back: खुद विचार किए बिना किसी की बात पर भरोसा कर लेना
cards.explain: जो लोग कान के कच्चे होते हैं, उनकी दोस्ती कभी लंबी नहीं चल पाती।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "पानी-पानी हो जाना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: सबके सामने झूठ पकड़े जाने पर विफल पानी-पानी हो गया।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "तूती बोलना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.back: बहुत मशहूर हो जाना, बहुत प्रभाव होना
cards.explain: अद्भुत खेल और खेल-भावना के कारण सचिन की संसार भर में तूती बोला करती थी।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "फूला न समाना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.explain: पूरे प्रांत में प्रथम आने पर मुदित फूला न समाया।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "आँखों का तारा" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "नाकों चने चबवाना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "कान पर जूँ न रेंगना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "नानी याद आना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "बाल बाँका न होना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "दाँतों तले उँगली दबाना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "छत्तीस का आँकड़ा" होने का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "घी के दीये जलाना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)

cards.front: "छक्के छुड़ाना" का अर्थ क्या है?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi grammar book (भाषा और व्याकरण), Ch 15 (pp. 128–137)
